purpose: IDP accuracy Lane B (directive 2026-10-25 section 7): six separate replacement definitions, in SHADOW. Changes no value, anchor, flag, scoring rule or served behaviour.

bestBallReproduction.note: Sleeper sums each player's points rounded to 2 decimals, so a total can differ from the unrounded sum by a few hundredths. A rostered player with no stat line scores 0.0 and is startable (the host's rule).

starterAllocation.note: season-to-date ppg lineups; attribution by slot family, FLEX/SUPER_FLEX by the occupant's own position (flex competition is measured, not preassigned)

bootstrap.intervalDefinition: ci95Conditional: percentile interval from resampling the played weeks of exactly the players behind each number (and teams as clusters for league-wide thresholds); conditional on the selected identities, so it excludes selection (winner's curse). reselection: spread of the whole definition when games are resampled and everything is re-selected; it is biased upward for maxima and is NOT an interval. identityStability: how often the same player or set sets the level again.

selectionRegression.rule: free agents ranked by ppg over weeks before w only; scored on week w

summary.mechanismNote: A planner allocation (maximises total lineup points gained, each free agent to at most one team). It is NOT a model of FAAB bids and does not predict who wins a contested player.

walkForward.rule: free agents, gains and the matching use weeks before w only; the claims are scored on week w alone
walkForward.caveat: three evaluation weeks and one allocation per week: an honest direction, not a precise ratio

averageWeekProjectionContrast.what: the same serial matching on one pseudo-week of empirical-Bayes expected ppg per player (an average-week lineup)

marginalBestBallContribution.unit: best-ball lineup points per week, whole-roster solve per week (never a sum of per-player deltas)

inSampleWeeks1to6.caution: the backfill is selected on the same weeks it is scored on, so it is optimistic and every over-replacement value is understated

walkForward.rule: for each evaluated week w the backfill is chosen from weeks < w only; its contribution is scored on week w alone

wholeRosterPackages.note: every number is a whole before/after roster solve; the naive sum is shown only to expose the interaction

consumerImpact.scope: OFFLINE shadow: anchor dicts swapped into the consumers' own pure functions; nothing written back, no flag changed

rosterCapacityAndTradeFinder.trade: each team gives its offense player nearest 3,500 and receives the next team's two (net +1) or three (net +2) offense players nearest 3,500 (Investigation B's neutral trade)

D6_teamSpecificAfterTheTrade.note: a position whose best claim is unpriced or helps nobody keeps the served anchor (counted, never zero)

faabVRepl.note: FAAB V_repl is position-agnostic and has its own anchor; only the pool it reads changes here

li5ConsolidationFlagOn_lensA.note: no schedule rows were supplied, so byes are not applied; the health step uses the cached players DB statuses only

consumerImpact.scarcityMultiplier: inert (1.0) at every position: the gameplan bundle still hands LI-5 no free agents, and none of the definitions here changes that

reproductionOfInvestigationB.method: Investigation B's script (scripts/idp_replacement_research.py, unmodified) was run on the pinned inputs; the shadow module in legacy-B mode (pools keyed by listed position, B's health rules, no games/production floor, value ordering, B's production bar) is compared field by field

limits: Six regular-season weeks (2026 weeks 1-6). A free agent's ppg is three to six games; single-player levels (D2 best, D4 rank 3) are noise-dominated and their intervals are wide.

The interval quoted is CONDITIONAL on the players who set each level; it excludes the selection itself. Free agents were chosen because their ppg was high, and the out-of-sample check shows the top five by history score roughly half (IDP) of it the next week. Read every free-agent level beside selectionRegression.

The game-level full-procedure bootstrap is biased upward for maxima and for lineup-optimised statistics; it is published only as selection stability (identity) and an inflation diagnostic, never as an interval.

In-sample lineup gains (D5, D6, packages, contributions over replacement) are hindsight: the backfill is chosen on the weeks it is scored on. The walk-forward blocks choose on weeks before the scored week; the allocation realised about a quarter of what history predicted.

The board prices only a minority of the productive free agents (unpricedViable). Value-unit D3/D4 levels therefore rest on very few priced players and are mostly undefined or near the board floor; an unpriced player is counted and never given a value of 0.

A DL/LB hybrid is legal at either slot by Sleeper's fantasy_positions (the exact solver's basis, verified against Sleeper's awarded best-ball totals); the eligibility-uncertainty block shows how much each level moves if hybrids were nominal only.

Health is a single snapshot (2026-10-25 20:15Z players DB: explicit status plus injury designation). A missing status is UNKNOWN. Bye weeks are inferred from the stat dumps for weeks 1-6 only; no forward schedule was used, so a future bye is not modelled.

D5 is a planner allocation (maximise total lineup points; each free agent to at most one team). It is not a model of FAAB bidding and does not say who wins a contested player. The cheapest legal drop is a rostered player who never starts, which is exact (adding a player cannot promote a non-starter) and free; this is the module's own lineup-points reading, not the production forced-drop owner.

Empirical-Bayes expectation uses a normal prior per (position, rostered or free agent). Free-agent populations are right-skewed mixtures, so it over-shrinks true risers; it brackets the raw level from below. It is validated out of sample for FREE AGENTS only (estimatorMse: lower squared error than raw); it is not published for rostered starters, where a rostered mean that includes bench players would pull stars down.

Consumer diagnostics swap anchor dicts into the consumers' own pure functions offline. They are not the served result: no flag was changed, and the displacement/capacity owners were read, never edited.

Investigation B's 2,156 DB anchor (an Out player) does not reproduce on the pinned 2026-10-25 inputs because the rosters moved; its code reproduces exactly on the new inputs (63 of 63 anchors), so the change is data, not method.
